settings.title: Settings
settings.soundsSub: Game and background can be switched separately
settings.fxTip: Switches the sounds of moves, bumps, Freeze, exits and wins. Background music is separate.
settings.ambientTip: Switches the music and ambient sounds of the chosen theme. Game action sounds are separate.
settings.ambientSub: The mood of the chosen theme
settings.arrowsTip: Below: a large D-pad under the board with the buttons beside it. Edges: the arrows sit on the board edges. None: no arrows, the buttons in one row under the board, so the board is largest; move by swiping on a phone, with the arrow keys or by dragging with the mouse on a computer. Without arrows, gesture control is always on.
settings.arrowsSub: Below · on the edges · no arrows
settings.gestureSub: On a touch screen you can also swipe on the board
settings.gestureTip: When on, swiping right, left, up or down on the board makes one move in that direction; one swipe is always one move. Tapping pieces (e.g. to select a Freeze target) still works. While on, the browser does not scroll, zoom or pull-to-refresh on the board. The phone’s own system gestures (such as back from the screen edge) still work, so swipe near the middle of the screen.
settings.motionSub: Tilt the phone, and optionally slide it, to move
settings.motionTip: On a phone you can move the pieces by tilting the device and, with a separate switch, by sliding it. Needs motion sensor permission.
settings.sensitivityTip: Applies to tilting and, if enabled, sliding. 1: needs a bigger motion; 10: a small motion is enough. One motion is at most one move.
settings.fastTiltTip: When on, the move happens during the tilt, not after the phone is tilted back. Tilting back never makes an opposite move, and quick consecutive tilts are not lost. When off, the earlier (v1) recognizer runs; sliding only works with that one.
settings.slideTip: When on, sliding the phone right, left, up or down in the plane of the screen also makes one move. When off, only tilting moves. Lifting and lowering never move.
settings.slideSub: When off, sliding does not move
settings.settleTip: The quiet time waited after a motion. 1: shorter wait; 10: longer. It does not change how fast pieces move.
settings.measureTip: Records test tilts, lifts, lowerings and slides into a JSON file. This is a research measurement; it does not tune motion control. The measurement screen is in Hungarian.
help.title: GGrid · Help
help.goal:
Goal

Get the ball out through the EXIT marked on the edge of the board. From the exit you still have to make one more move in the direction shown. Every direction command moves all movable pieces at once: walls do not move, and joined blocks move together. On two-ball levels (●● in the Level box) both balls must get out.
help.controls:
Controls

Arrows: the large arrow buttons under the board make one move; hold them to repeat. On a computer the keyboard arrow keys work too.

Swipe: on a touch screen swipe right, left, up or down on the board to move; one swipe is always one move. While on, the browser does not scroll or zoom on the board. It can be turned off under Settings → Gesture control (not in the no-arrows layout).

Tilt: on a phone it can be turned on under Settings → Motion control. Fast tilt recognition moves during the motion; sliding (moving the phone in its plane) can be enabled separately. Sensitivity and the delay that closes a motion are adjustable.

Arrow layout (Settings → Interface): Below – a large D-pad under the board; Edges – arrows on the board edges; None – no arrows, the buttons in one row under the board, so the board is largest. Without arrows you move by swiping on a phone, and with the arrow keys or by dragging with the mouse on a computer; gesture control is then always on.
help.buttons:
Buttons under the board

Left (first in the row in the no-arrows layout): ❄ Freeze, 💣 BOMB, 💡 hint. Right: ↶ restart, ⟳ new level, ▦ level select. At the top: the ☰ menu, the moves (made / optimal; after a bomb the optimum shows “–”), the difficulty and size of the level, and your points.

Short messages on the board (for example “Freeze used”, “Blown up”) disappear after 2 seconds or at your next move.
help.levels:
Choosing levels

In Free play you can select any number of sizes and difficulties (D1–D10), in any combination; tap to switch them on and off. The summary line shows how many levels match. The game draws from all level libraries, mixing one- and two-ball levels, and offers levels you have not solved yet first.

Themes: browse the themes and use the ✓ Selected / + Add switch in the corner to choose which ones you want; All and Only this are quick choices. Every new level gets a random theme from the selected ones; restarting keeps the theme.

Adaptive difficulty: if several difficulties are selected, the game chooses among them by your performance. It tracks your level (separately for one- and two-ball levels), starts at the easiest selected difficulty, and mostly offers levels around and slightly above your level. Good solutions raise your level; weaker results lower it gently. A level’s result is the ratio of optimal to actual moves; hints lower it, the automatic solution counts as zero, and a level solved with a bomb does not count. Asking for a new level without solving after at least 5 moves counts as a failure; skipping after a quick look and restarting do not. Your level is shown in the level select and its change on the victory card; the Reset button starts it over, and the switch turns it off.
help.points:
Points

Both one- and two-ball levels give points. A level’s value depends on its size, difficulty and optimal number of moves; two-ball levels give a small bonus for handling two balls. An optimal solution earns the full value, more moves earn less, but at least half. On the same level you only earn new points for improving on your previous best. If you used a BOMB on a level, solving it earns a fixed 5 points and the level does not count as solved. Points and solved levels are stored in your browser.
help.aids:
Aids

A short press on 💡 shows the next move from the current position for 1 point. The direction is shown by a highlighted label (for example ↑ UP), and the matching arrow button under the board pulses (in the no-arrows layout a large arrow pulses on that edge of the board); the advice stays until your next move, at most 8 seconds. Asking again without moving shows the same advice for free; after a move, a restart or a new level it costs 1 point again. If there is no solution without Freeze, it looks for one that uses at most one Freeze and names the piece to freeze. Holding it for 2 seconds shows the solution step by step, with Freeze if needed.

Automatic solution: its status is shown in the bar under the board. The red ✕ stops it at any time, and you can continue from where it stopped. If you started it on a level, that run earns no points even if you finish it by hand; after a restart you can earn points again. If there is no solution to be found from that position, the game tells you.

The ❄ Freeze button enters selection mode. Tap the ball or movable piece to hold in place; tap it again to clear, or tap another to move the selection. Press Freeze again to leave without cost. With a piece selected, the next direction command costs 10 points even if nothing moves; then Freeze mode ends. Below 10 points the button is not available.

The 💣 BOMB button enters blast mode (with a mouse, a crosshair shows over the board); tap a piece to remove it for 15 points: it disappears in an explosion and the board shakes. Walls and movable blocks can be blown up, balls and the exit cannot, and a multi-cell block disappears as a whole. Press BOMB again to leave without cost; a direction command also ends blast mode. Below 15 points the button is not available. After a bomb the level is worth a fixed 5 points, does not count as solved and does not change your level; a restart brings back the original level and full points can be earned again.
help.sound:
Sound and menu

In Settings, game action sounds and the theme’s background sound can be switched separately. From the ☰ menu you can restart, ask for a new level, open the settings or this help, or return to the main screen.
